boundaries: This scenario combines exact captured source text with an explicitly saved process declaration. The Dashboard-to-Places interaction is agent-proposed; runtime target binding, request completion, transaction durability after timeout, publisher activation, Kafka routing and downstream delivery are not verified. The diagram expresses a source-based narrative, not guaranteed runtime ordering.
Syntax evidence does not establish runtime dispatch or configuration. Expand known owners and helpers; retain explicit gaps for unresolved targets.

events.text: A caller enters savePlace with a JSON body. The declared Places request body requires only cityId, a string in the oslo, helsinki, or lisbon enum; SavePlace exposes that value as CityId.

Dashboard POSTs JSON.stringify(request.body) to /places with content-type application/json and AbortSignal.timeout(10000). The saved interaction is an agent-proposed target mapping, not proof of runtime routing.
Places returns HTTP 400 with error UNSUPPORTED_CITY.
For a supported city, repository.Save opens a connection, begins a transaction, and inserts the place with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING id.
The place INSERT returns a new id
Within the same transaction, InsertRequest creates a UUID and inserts a JSONB outbox payload with type place.requested, version 1, and the place.
If the INSERT returns null after a conflict, InsertRequest is skipped, so this call adds no outbox row.
repository.Save commits the transaction after the optional outbox insert; the new place and its outbox row share that transaction.
After repository.Save returns, the controller returns HTTP 200 with the mapped city.
Dashboard forwards the upstream status and parsed JSON body. The shown Places branches return 400 for an unsupported city or 200 after a supported save.
A fetch or response.json exception, including an abort from the 10-second signal, is caught and mapped to HTTP 503 PLACES_UNAVAILABLE.

The exception may occur before or after Places commits, so this 503 is not a database outcome. The handler has no retry branch. A later call can follow the no-outbox conflict path whenever the place INSERT returns null, including for a preexisting city or another request; the source does not identify which request caused that state.

The saved process links the Places publisher, Forecasts consumer/publisher, and Dashboard consumer views as separate subviews. This HTTP narrative does not establish their activation, routing, retry behavior, or message delivery, and the outbox insert is not a synchronous broker acknowledgement.

rows.label: Request
rows.value: The declared required JSON body is an object with no additional properties and one required cityId string, restricted to oslo, helsinki, or lisbon.

rows.label: Declared responses
rows.value: The OpenAPI operation declares a 200 Place JSON object and a 400 JSON error object, plus 415 and 500 status codes. The captured controller explicitly returns 400 for an unsupported mapping and 200 after repository.Save; the declaration does not prove runtime enforcement or exception-to-status mapping.

rows.value: The saved process records Dashboard.savePlace to Places.Save as an agent-proposed POST /places interaction. Runtime receiver binding and routing remain unverified.

summary.text: A caller submits a cityId to Dashboard.savePlace. The handler serializes the body and sends POST /places with a 10-second abort signal; the declared OpenAPI request is an object containing only cityId, with oslo, helsinki, and lisbon as allowed values. The saved Dashboard-to-Places mapping is agent-proposed, so runtime target binding is not established. Places returns 400 UNSUPPORTED_CITY when its city mapping fails; otherwise it awaits repository.Save and returns 200. Save inserts the place in a database transaction, inserts a place.requested version 1 outbox record only when the place insert returns a new id, and commits. A conflict skips the outbox insert but still commits. Dashboard forwards a parsed upstream status/body, while a fetch or JSON parse exception returns 503 PLACES_UNAVAILABLE; the wrapper has no retry and that response does not say whether the Places transaction committed. The no-outbox path is tied to the place INSERT returning null on conflict; that can reflect an existing city or another request, so it is not a retry guarantee for the timed-out caller. The saved process links publisher and consumer views separately; an outbox row is not proof of Kafka publication or consumption.
